title: pvExtractSubset
body:
## pvExtractSubset

Extracts a sub-block of a structured dataset (image data, rectilinear or curvilinear grid) by point-index ranges in I, J and K, optionally keeping only every n-th index; the output has the same structured type. Use it to crop or coarsen a structured grid cheaply, e.g. one K-plane of a 3-D grid. Use extractSubset for the same operation with Schemaxis defaults (includeBoundary true).

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- VOI uses point indices in the input's extent, which need not start at 0; check the input extent first.
- With sample rates above 1 the last index is dropped unless IncludeBoundary is true.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `ExtractSubset`. Identity: `filters/ExtractGrid`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Extract Grid filter. Accepted data: image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid); structured points (image data) (vtkStructuredPoints); curvilinear structured grids (vtkStructuredGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid","vtkStructuredPoints","vtkStructuredGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IncludeBoundary` | If the value of this property is 1, then if the sample rate in any dimension is greater than 1, the boundary indices of the input dataset will be passed to the output even if the boundary extent is not an even multiple of the sample rate in a given dimension. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `SampleRateI` | This property indicates the sampling rate in the I dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `SampleRateJ` | This property indicates the sampling rate in the J dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `SampleRateK` | This property indicates the sampling rate in the K dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `VOI` | This property specifies the minimum and maximum point indices along each of the I, J, and K axes; these values indicate the volume of interest (VOI). The output will have the (I,J,K) extent specified here. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvExtractSubset",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
